# Bidline Launch Blueprint v1.0.0

**Status:** draft · **Implementation:** PROPOSED · **Kind:** existing niche · **Created:** 2026-11-10T03:00:00Z
**Source brief:** brief_bidline_v1-0-0 v1.0.0 (draft), `sha256:015257e1bba9…`
**Generated by:** @forge/builder 1.0.0 (deterministic) · **Auto-launch:** never

> A blueprint is a plan. Nothing in it is built, tested or live until a build stage records independent gate receipts. Launch always needs the owner's explicit approval.

## Decision from the brief

**go with changes**: Bidline paid Estimating Kit. Real, large audience and verified spreadsheet behaviour, plus paid bundles at $9-$109 on Etsy and Gumroad. But the free-template market is saturated and earlier FORGE research ranked a trades estimate pack last. Proceed only with a differentiated kit; keep investment small until first-party sales prove demand.

Falsifying test: If the kit is live, checkout works and Bidline gets at least 300 organic sessions to the kit page within 60 days of launch with zero sales, move Bidline to hold and shift Stage 2 to Quilt Plan Kit. Thresholds are owner-adjustable decision rules, not forecasts.

## Positioning

Small US residential contractors do price jobs in spreadsheets and lose money on markup, overhead and labour-hour mistakes, but basic estimate templates are given away free by software vendors and dozens of AI-built sites, so Bidline only earns money if its paid kit sells the profit loop (overhead recovery, labour hours, estimate vs actual) rather than a template.

| Segment | Priority |
|---|---|
| Owner-operator residential contractor (target) | primary |
| New or second-year contractor | secondary |
| Single-trade specialist (roofing, electrical, landscaping) | exploratory |

## Products

### Bidline Estimate-to-Profit Kit (`prd_bidline_estimate-to-profit-kit`)

core tier · $19 (INFERRED) · playbook `spreadsheet-template` · PROPOSED · builds on registry `prd_bidline_kit`

Format: Excel workbook (also opens in Google Sheets) + one-page quick-start PDF + filled example job

Must include:
- Overhead recovery: monthly overhead / billable hours = true hourly cost
- Labour hours by phase x rate, separate from materials
- Reusable unit-cost price book the estimate pulls from
- Correct pricing by target margin, with markup shown alongside
- Estimate vs actual job-cost tab that flags misses and feeds the price book
- Change-order log
- Client-ready printable quote page
- A complete worked example (e.g. a 12x16 deck) so it is useful in 10 minutes

Must not:
- Be the free template renamed (the current paid file is byte-identical to the free one, per WS3)
- Claim it guarantees profit or wins bids
- Require macros (blocked in Google Sheets and many Excel setups)

Deliverables:
- **workbook** (xlsx): Styled to the brand; inputs unlocked, formulas protected; no macros; opens in Excel and Google Sheets without errors.
- **quick-start** (pdf): One page: what it does, how to fill it in, where the answer appears.
- **worked-example** (xlsx): Filled example using realistic, labelled sample inputs (never presented as a customer).
- **formula-test-cases** (json): ≥5 known input/output cases checked by an independent reviewer (G4).

Gates: G4, G5, G6, G7, G8, G13

Falsifying test: Zero sales from the first 300 organic sessions on the kit page within 60 days of checkout going live means the offer or audience is wrong; hold and re-research.

### Trade edition or kit + trade price-book bundle (`prd_bidline_trade-edition-or-kit-trade-price-book-bundle`)

premium tier · $39 (INFERRED) · playbook `bundle` · PROPOSED

Format: Bundle of products (reused or built in this build)

Deliverables:
- **bundle-manifest** (json): Lists every component (existing products and any new item built for the bundle) with file hashes; every component passes G4 on its own.
- **bundle-archive** (zip): Delivered archive equals the reviewed archive (hash match).

Gates: G4, G5, G6, G7, G8, G13

## Sales framework (Promise, Pain, Proof, Plan, Picture)

**Promise (draft):** Know the real margin on every job before sending the quote.
  - basis: Know the real margin on every job before sending the quote. _[INFERRED, c_bl_out_margin]_

**Pain:**
- Confusing markup with margin, which underprices jobs (30% markup is about 23% margin). _[VERIFIED, c_bl_pain_markup]_
- Not spreading overhead across billable hours, so small jobs lose money. _[VERIFIED, c_bl_pain_overhead]_
- Material price volatility makes old price sheets wrong. _[VERIFIED, c_bl_pain_materials]_
- Estimating eats evenings; contractors want it faster. _[VERIFIED, c_bl_pain_time]_

**Proof:** has candidates. No testimonials, ratings, sales counts, user numbers or results until they exist and are verified.
Allowed kinds:
- Previews rendered from the real product files
- Worked example with clearly labelled sample data
- Verified facts from the brief, cited
- Customer feedback only once it exists, with permission

Verified facts the page may cite (these are not testimonials):
- Contractors describe building exactly these components themselves. _[VERIFIED, c_bl_pp_e1]_

**Plan:**
1. Get the Bidline Estimate-to-Profit Kit for $19
2. Download it straight from the confirmation email
3. Start with: Overhead recovery: monthly overhead / billable hours = true hourly cost

**Picture (draft):** Win more of the jobs worth winning without racing to the bottom.

**Call to action:** Get the Bidline Estimate-to-Profit Kit

**Objections to answer on the page:**
- "I can get an estimate template free from Housecall Pro or Google." _[VERIFIED, c_bl_obj_free]_
- "Should I just use Joist or Jobber?" (free tiers exist). _[VERIFIED, c_bl_obj_app]_
- "A generic template won't match my trade." _[INFERRED, c_bl_obj_fit]_

**Customer language:**
- “I lose leads when I quote high, and make less than I expected when I go lower.”
- “Material unit costs on one sheet, labour hours by phase on another.”
- “Compare every estimate to the final cost.”
- “Why is a 30% markup not a 30% margin?”

## Brand

Direction from the brief:
- Contractors respond to practical, plain, job-site language and real worked examples over corporate software styling. _[INFERRED, c_bl_vis_practical]_
- Excel familiarity, offline use and easy PDF export are reasons contractors keep spreadsheets over apps. _[VERIFIED, c_bl_vis_excel]_

Requirements:
- Designed for this audience, distinct from the other FORGE niches; no generic AI layout
- Licensed or original imagery only, each asset recorded in SOURCES_AND_LICENSES.md
- Accessible type and contrast (WCAG 2.2 AA); readable at 320 px
- Real product previews rendered from the actual files
- Products styled to the same standard as the site that sells them

Unknown provenance is a G8 FAIL. No asset ships without source URL, author, licence, commercial-use terms and attribution recorded.

## Budget and permissions

Budget ceiling: not set (owner to set). Spend authorized: no. A ceiling is a limit, not permission to buy.

Allowed without asking:
- Local development and tests
- Generating product files and previews
- Staging preview deploys
- Draft content and copy
- Test-mode checkout once the owner has connected the account
- Writing FORGE database records for this build

Needs the owner's approval:
- Production deploy or launch
- New accounts or credential connections
- Any purchase or subscription
- Turning on live checkout
- Price changes
- Publishing outside approved campaigns
- Changes to customer data or permissions

Never:
- Fabricated testimonials, reviews, sales counts or results
- Unlicensed images, fonts or text
- Copying another designer's or competitor's work
- Spam, purchased lists or prohibited scraping
- Storing secrets in the repo or dashboard
- Writing sales rows to the ledger
- Touching businesses outside FORGE

- All launch_readiness gates PASS with independent receipts
- Owner has explicitly approved the launch
